stimulus.text: Paraphrase: In June 1941, President Franklin D. Roosevelt issued Executive Order 8802. The order banned discrimination in defense industries and in government training programs because of race, creed, color, or national origin. It also created the Fair Employment Practices Committee to receive and investigate complaints. The order came after the labor leader A. Philip Randolph, head of the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, threatened a large march on Washington to protest discrimination in war jobs.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Executive Order 8802, June 25, 1941. Randolph's threatened March on Washington, planned for July 1941, was called off after the order.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Executive Order 8802 (June 25, 1941)
stem: The order banned discrimination in defense work, yet Black workers still faced discrimination during the war. Which of the following best explains that gap?

options.text: The order applied only to workers in the South
options.misconception: The order covered defense industries across the country.

options.text: The order was overturned by the Supreme Court in 1942
options.misconception: The Court never overturned Executive Order 8802.

options.text: The order banned Black workers from skilled jobs
options.misconception: The order banned discrimination; it did not impose it.

options.text: The committee enforcing the order had little power to punish employers

rationales.A: The ban covered defense industries everywhere, not only in the South.
rationales.B: No court struck the order down; it stayed in force through the war.
rationales.C: The order's words ban discrimination, so they cannot explain discrimination continuing.
rationales.D: Background: the Fair Employment Practices Committee could investigate complaints but could not force an employer to hire.
rationales.general:
1. A rule on paper only works if someone can enforce it.
2. The order created a committee to receive and investigate complaints.
3. Background: that committee could investigate, but it had no power to punish an employer that refused to hire.
4. So many employers kept old hiring habits, and change came slowly.
Remember: a ban without enforcement is a promise, not a result; check who enforces it.
